body: This seems like it shouldn't be here.
Another case that would be good to test: subquery where the range is longer than the query step (eg. this test case, but with Interval set to a minute)
There's another "phase 3" comment three test cases earlier - do we need both groups of tests?
A lot of these new tests seem very similar, or it's not clear what they're exercising in contrast to other tests.

This isn't correct: there isn't a 1:1 mapping between the child query steps and the parent query steps.
For example, if we're evaluating an instant query at T=25m with the expression sum_over_time(foo[10m:1m]), then the single parent query step should include all the samples read for 10 inner steps, from T=16m to T=25m. (The left boundary is not inclusive.)
Furthermore, if we're evaluating a range query containing a subquery, then the value of SamplesReadPerStep for each parent step should only include samples read in the child query that haven't been included in a previous parent step. This would keep the behaviour consistent with range vector selectors.
For example, if the expression is sum_over_time(foo[10m:1m]), evaluated from T=25m to T=29m with a 2m step, then the first parent step (T=25m) should include all the samples read for 10 inner steps, then T=27m and T=29m should only include the new samples read (2 inner steps each).

Shouldn't this be 1 sample read?
This is an instant query evaluated at T=90s, and the subquery has a 30s range with a 30s step.
The left boundary of a subquery is not included, so the only step returned by the subquery is at T=90s. metricWith1SampleEvery10Seconds has one series, and there is a sample within the lookback window, so the instant vector selector returns a single sample and so this counts as one sample read.
I think this might have uncovered a separate bug: why is there an inner step beyond the last one required for the outer query?
Shouldn't this be 3? At T=261s, the subquery will read a sample at T=240s, T=250s and T=260s.

If this was unknown to the callee would the value be zero?
If so, there much value in checking?
Ideally this would be in a separate PR, as it is unrelated to this one.
